chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no one dying from among the believers whose death is more beloved to Iblis than the death of a faqih.

key_terms.إِبْلِيسَ: Iblis — the name of Satan/the Devil in the Quran; the one who refused to bow before Adam and vowed to mislead humanity
key_terms.فَقِيهٍ: faqih — a scholar deeply versed in Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh); in Shia context, one qualified to derive religious rulings and guide the community

ai.seo_question: Why does the death of a scholar (faqih) bring joy to Iblis according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares that among all the deaths of believers, the death of a faqih (Islamic jurist) is the event most beloved to Iblis. This hadith underscores the pivotal role of the religious scholar in preserving faith and guiding the community — when a faqih dies, Satan celebrates because a guardian of sacred knowledge and religious practice has been lost. The original audience, early Shia Muslims facing political persecution under the Abbasid caliphate, would have understood this as a strong exhortation to value, protect, and support their scholars.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no one dying from the Momineen (whose death) is more beloved to Iblees<sup>la</sup> than the death of an understanding one (فَقِيهٍ)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Sulayman ibn Khalid from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “
Of the deaths of the true believers the one that Satan loves most is the death of a Faqih, one who has very good understand of religion and its laws.”
